title: Express Asynchronous Error Swallowing & Hanging Socket Leak
businessContext: In an Express.js REST API handling merchant inventory updates, when an unexpected database constraint error occurs inside an async route handler, the client request hangs indefinitely until hitting a 60-second gateway timeout. Over time, open socket handles accumulate, exhausting file descriptors.
problemStatement: Express 4 does not automatically catch rejected promises returned from `async (req, res, next)` route handlers. When an unhandled error throws inside an async function without an explicit `next(err)` or wrapper, Express never sends an HTTP response, leaving the client socket hanging open.
constraints: Must guarantee every rejected promise in route handlers is caught and passed to global error middleware.
Must return consistent RFC 7807 Problem Details JSON format `{ status: 500, title, detail }`.
Prevent socket handle and file descriptor exhaustion.
candidateTasks: Explain why Express 4 fails to catch rejected promises in async middleware.
Implement an `asyncHandler` higher-order function that wraps async routes with `.catch(next)`.
Discuss how Express 5 natively handles rejected promises.
hints: Express 4 route handlers expect synchronous code or explicit `next(err)` invocations.
Create a wrapper: `const asyncHandler = fn => (req, res, next) => Promise.resolve(fn(req, res, next)).catch(next)`.

testCases.name: Catches async exceptions and routes to global error handler
testCases.explanation: Guarantees proper response termination on async exceptions.

alternativeApproaches: Upgrading to Express 5 or migrating to Fastify / Koa (which have native promise support).
commonMistakes: Writing manual try/catch in every single route handler (repetitive and prone to human omission).
Placing the 4-argument error middleware `(err, req, res, next)` BEFORE route definitions (it must be registered last).
